rule_CROSS-1: For the same occasion+season, the top-3 looks of any two house chips must not share a core key (top.id|bottom.id|shoe.id). The chip with the stronger fingerprint score for that core keeps it; the other drops to its next valid look.
rule_CROSS-2: Across all chips' top-3 for one context, a dominant plate (see dominance) appears in at most 2 chips.
rule_CROSS-3: RRL, Polo, Purple and ItalianSummer rows must never equal the All row. If a house has <3 valid looks, show fewer cards + the gap note; never pad from All.

rules: ≤1 per 8-look row per plate (Sweet Stable cords ≤2)
≤1 dominant plate in the top-3 of a chip
−25 soft penalty per use (−15 for SS cords)
a dominant plate may be #1 only if no non-dominant look passes

must_differ_pairs.slot_rule: shoe: RRL boot vs Polo loafer/sneaker (Polo boot only with OCBD/knit + chino/cord/wool); top: work shirt vs OCBD/polo/cable.
top: RRL work shirt/henley vs SS gingham/fair isle/cable; bottom: RRL jean/chino vs SS cord. Both may use the one boot, so the core must differ on top AND bottom.
IW requires a jacket + fine knit + wool/cord + suede loafer and bans piqué/sneakers; Polo's top-3 should lead with OCBD/piqué/cable.
Faloni: knit polo/linen + pale trouser + suede loafer/mule; Polo: no mules, OCBD/piqué + chino/cord.
IS needs a soft jacket or an all-tonal core; mule only with a jacket. On a shared core, Faloni keeps the jacketless version.
545 bottom = denim or dark/relaxed trouser, top = henley/zip/knit polo; Faloni bottom = pale trouser.
545 bans NB and hoodies (except Comfy) and allows loafers; ALD bans loafers.
Purple uses a soft blazer (taupe/ivory/cord) + lighter bottoms; IW uses navy blazer/shearling/suede + dark wool.
IW bans boots, fair isle and plaid; SS bans city blazers and woven loafers.

test_cases.desc: Faloni and IS both surface Brown knit polo + ivory pleated + brown suede loafers in Out/Summer top-3
test_cases.resolution: Faloni keeps the jacketless look; IS takes its next core (e.g. Blue linen shirt + cream pleated + suede loafers + ivory DB).
